facts.text: Stanford, California, takes its name from the university founded in 1885 by railroad magnate Leland Stanford and his wife Jane to honor their son.
In the 1920s, former president Herbert Hoover helped stabilize Stanford’s finances and founded the Hoover Institution on War, Revolution and Peace in 1919.
Postwar years saw Stanford become a hub for electronics and computing precursors, driving the surrounding community’s shift from rural to tech‑adjacent.
The Stanford CDP remains unincorporated, while most of the university campus lies within it; the Stanford Shopping Center and Research Park belong to Palo Alto.
Stanford’s climate features warm, dry summers with average highs never exceeding 77.6 °F and cool, wet winters that stay above 37.7 °F.
